subject: history
title: Settling disputes, and equality for all

nodes: Limited resources: land, fresh water, coal, petroleum
Growing demands from a growing population
Conflict, e.g. states sharing river waters
props.label: Why conflicts arise, p.26

scenes.narration: Natural resources like land, fresh water, coal and petroleum are limited, but demands keep increasing because of our growing population. When resources are limited but demands many, there is conflict.

nodes: The police: law and order every day
props.label: Conflict resolution, p.26

scenes.narration: Conflict resolution is the peaceful settlement of disputes. The judiciary is the main body that deals with it, because the court is impartial. The police, and dialogue and negotiations, also help.

nodes: All equal in the eyes of the law, even top leaders
Laws against discrimination by caste, creed or colour
props.label: Equality and justice, pp.26–27

scenes.narration: In a democracy, all are equal in the eyes of the law, including leaders in the highest positions. In India, seats are reserved for people discriminated against for centuries, and laws prohibit discrimination on the basis of caste, creed or colour.

questions.prompt: Conflicts arise when resources are limited but the demands on them are many.
hints: Read the chart from top to bottom.

questions.prompt: In a democracy, are top leaders above the law?
options: No, all are equal in the eyes of the law
questions.answer: No, all are equal in the eyes of the law
